S.FORM: Ba nēk m-vit min na sur / kak am̄o, am̄o, ra ta Lkon va-vvōr, ra sul ta Lkon?
S.TRANSL: [Q] Did you say that in the old days, Gaua had a huge population?

S.FORM: Am̄o, ra sul ta Lkon va-vvōr.
S.TRANSL: Oh yes, in the old days, the island of Gaua had a huge population.

S.FORM: La sur, kak i tsik s-mat, na s-van sag na s-van sur Wrisris, kmār s-van le va nen̄, Wrisris ron̄: “Tuan̄ gēn sa m-mat le. La nēr / tuar tdun a-vre m-wōr ni.” Na s-van kēl ma na s-wōr bas nēr o si tdun nen̄.
S.TRANSL: But then, should my brother die, I’d walk in and go see Wrisris; I’d walk with him to that place in there, and he’d say “That brother of yours is dead. Someone in the village killed him.” And then I would immediately come back and kill him with all his descendants.

S.FORM: M̄rag nēr le gvur sutwal ak nēr – bul-vēs? Bul-san̄vul le –
S.TRANSL: Imagine how many there were in each family – how many people? ten, perhaps?

S.FORM: Na s-wōr bas nēr nēr s-mat.
S.TRANSL: But then I’d use sorcery and wipe them all out.

S.FORM: Titi m-daw tm̄a a Lkon sa, dek gēn nēk s-tek tm̄a Lkon sa, tm̄a s-vēs wor nok.
S.TRANSL: And this is how here on Gaua, if you look around here on Gaua, you can see there aren’t many people left.

S.FORM: Dek gēn t-bon̄ galāg gēn nok dek ti. Am̄o, m-van ma o tdun obek.
S.TRANSL: Well, right now, we have come back to a decent number. But before this, we had reached a point where people had almost disappeared.

S.FORM: Sur o wōr gēn sa le.
S.TRANSL: And the reason for this was black sorcery.

S.FORM: Na s-van sag na s-vārus, m-mat wor mi o sm̄an, va-wē.
S.TRANSL: For if I walked in and enquired, if it turned out the death was just due to sickness, that was fine.

S.FORM: La kak m-wōr, ti na s-van kēl ma na s-wōr kēl ra sē sa ka nēr ka m-wōr na / Na s-ram kēl wor ra titsik nen̄ sa nēr ka m-wōr ni.
S.TRANSL: But then if it was sorcery, then I’d come back and cast spells back on those who had killed me / I’d avenge my brother who was murdered that way.

S.FORM: Vetm̄e dek gēn le. 🌿
S.TRANSL: That’s how it was. 🌿

S.FORM: Titi ra ta Lkon nēr me-tger?
S.TRANSL: [Q] Is that what caused the depopulation of Gaua?

S.FORM: Tawe tdun a Lkon sa, m-bas. Nēr (ka) m-mat bas.
S.TRANSL: [A] Many people died on this island of Gaua. They all disappeared.

S.FORM: Ave? Kēl ave? Kēl barbar?
S.TRANSL: [Q] Where exactly? On the east coast?

S.FORM: Me-qtēg ka / me-qtēg aē sa, m-van tm̄e seg; van wālōg Lkon.
S.TRANSL: [A] It started here, and then went on and on all around the island.

S.FORM: Nēk s-van a Lkon sa nēk s-tek o tētne gvur olbaot, le m̄ōs, sur kēlkēl sur le m̄ōs sa, nēk s-tek o tētne vre sur le m̄ōs gēs sēg, o tdun t-aē gēn nen̄ m-mat bas le.
S.TRANSL: If you walk around Gaua, you’ll see remains of houses everywhere in the bush; if you follow the traces in the bush, you’ll see traces of entire villages scattered around: those were the people who disappeared in those times.

S.FORM: La m-van ma aqri, ti dek gēn tm̄a t-bon̄ galāg kēl ti.
S.TRANSL: Nowadays it’s different, our numbers have picked up again a little.

S.FORM: La am̄o va, o tdun m-bas nok. 🌿
S.TRANSL: But in the past, we did go through massive losses. 🌿

S.FORM: Ba Wrisris sa, ni m-togtog mumul?
S.TRANSL: [Q] So that Wrisris, did he live long?

S.FORM: Ni m-togtog mumul.
S.TRANSL: [A] Oh yes, he lived very long.

S.FORM: M-bas, ni me-tger mlē? ni me-tger [nan̄ēs]?
S.TRANSL: [Q] So then he died? Where did he die?

S.FORM: Ni me-tger a Bētās, le mon o vre.
S.TRANSL: He passed away by lake Betaas, where he had lived.

S.FORM: Sur sa?
S.TRANSL: [Q] Why?

S.FORM: Ni m-mat.
S.TRANSL: [A] He died.

S.FORM: Ni m-mat. Sē m-wōr nē?
S.TRANSL: [Q] Oh, he died. Was he murdered?

S.FORM: Bek. Ni m-mat wor srēg ka, ni me-tmarga, ni so mat.
S.TRANSL: [A] No, no. He just died a natural death: he had become old, and then he died.

S.FORM: La ni m-tog, ni m-tog ni m-tog ni m-tog mumul! O taw va-bon̄ va-bon̄ soqsoq.
S.TRANSL: But before that, he had lived for a very, very long time. For many many years.

S.FORM: O tdun t-wotwot wōn wor ni ti, t-mat ti, Wrisris t-tog ti.
S.TRANSL: For generations and generations, Wrisris was present when people were born, and still present when they died.

S.FORM: Avvan, ni m-tog avvan, me-tmarga rōrōw ni so mat.
S.TRANSL: He lived all this time, for very very long, until he became so old that he finally passed away.

S.FORM: Ba ni so mat, ra wed / ratle wed m-van nok ma, le?
S.TRANSL: [Q] When he died, had White people already come here?

S.FORM: Ratle Wetman / ratle tdun wedwed, m-van nok ma.
S.TRANSL: [A] Yes. Some White people had already come here.

S.FORM: Ra dōn t-van dēn̄ t' gin ni. 🌿
S.TRANSL: Some of them even had visited him personally. 🌿

S.FORM: Tuar qōn̄, nēk s-van sag kak ni obek, m̄rag tuar o tdun vi-lwo rōw ka t-tog t' aē.
S.TRANSL: Certain days, you would go up and not find him; instead, his place would be taken by some important chief.

S.FORM: T-van dēn̄ t' gin ni, ron̄ “Ni obek sa! Ni m-van le vara Wetman.”
S.TRANSL: You’d walk all the way to that chief, who would tell you “Wrisris is not here. He’s gone to the land of the White.”

S.FORM: M̄rag le susrig ka nami Wrisris ron̄, Wrisris dēn̄ ta Ostrelia.
S.TRANSL: That’s a well known story, that Wrisris went all the way to Australia.

S.FORM: Ostrelia arās, Wrisris t-van ti ni t-van aksavm̄ag ti?
S.TRANSL: Australia is very far, so how could Wrisris even go there?

S.FORM: O plēn obek, sur s-la ni s-van, nēr s-tek tēmē kak ni s-van lul a mke ak.
S.TRANSL: There was no plane that he could fly in then. And nobody ever saw him on a ship!

S.FORM: Wrisris ni tuar tdun sa – ni o tdun la, tuar qōn̄ ni s-van nēk te tek late ni ni t-van ti.
S.TRANSL: That’s the sort of person Wrisris was. He was just a man, but some days he would just become invisible and travel.

S.FORM: Tuar qōn̄ nēr s-van kēl sag nēr s-mōl kēl ma ron̄ “Wrisris m-mōl kēl nok ma!” 🌿
S.TRANSL: And then another day, people would walk back up there, and returning to the village they’d say “Wrisris is back!” 🌿

S.FORM: Nē m-van ma ave? Nē ta Lkon? (i Wrisris)
S.TRANSL: [Q] Where was Wrisris from? Was he a native of Gaua?

S.FORM: Wrisris ni ta Lkon, ni m-wot a Lkon: a Mke-Grāt, a tāvtēn t-aē.
S.TRANSL: [A] Wrisris was from Gaua, he was born on Gaua: on the Ghraat volcano, just underneath it.

S.FORM: Le qōtgi grāt, o grāt a mken, aa? a tāvtēn t-aē. Namon o tne vre a tāvtēn t-aē.
S.TRANSL: You see the volcano rising high above, right? well, he was born underneath, at the foot of the hill. His place is at the foot of the volcano.

S.FORM: Ni s-togtog, nintēg tuar o wasn̄in a Diwtag.
S.TRANSL: More precisely, he lived in a place called Diwtagh.

S.FORM: Diwtag?
S.TRANSL: [Q] Diwtagh?

S.FORM: Diwtag. Na ssa tuar o wasn̄in. O tne vre aē. Diwtag.
S.TRANSL: [A] Diwtagh. It’s the name of a place. It used to be a village. Diwtagh.

S.FORM: 🌿 / Va-wē wor. Va-wē adad!
S.TRANSL: Great. Thank you! 🌿
